newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo Bourse chief unruffled by Sysdeco aff.
newsitem.headline: Oslo Bourse chief unruffled by Sysdeco aff.

text.p: Repercussions of the Morgan Grenfell affair in Norway have not hurt investors' confidence in the Oslo stock exchange, Bourse Director Kjell Froensdal said on Wednesday.
Last week Deutsche Bank AG said that it, together with London-based investment subsidiary Morgan Grenfell Asset Management Ltd (MGAM), owned 51 percent of Norwegian software house Sysdeco ASA.
Norwegian newspapers had speculated the affair would make foreign investors pull out of the Oslo market, one of the smallest in Europe, but Froensdal remained confident.
"The big players are professional enough to know that these things can happen in a stock market. We have to live with it," he said.

The Deutsche Bank announcement raised eyebrows in Oslo because Norwegian securities regulations call for a company to make an offer to the remaining shareholders once it has acquired 45 percent or more of the issued equity in a concern.
Following the announcement, bourse authorities transferred Sysdeco to a watch list pending further information.
"I am still not familiar enough with the details of the matter but as far as I know such a thing could happen in any market," Froensdal said.
"This is also shown by the Morgan Grenfell case, which has connections in a lot of countries and markets."
He said Oslo Bourse was discussing with Deutsche Bank how MGAM was able to buy such a major stake in Sysdeco.
"We have a positive dialogue going with Deutsche Bank, and we hope for an early clarification of the facts."

Froensdal said it was difficult to control who at any one time was ultimately behind a transaction on the bourse. It would take rigid regulations to ensure 100 percent control and that in turn could frighten away foreign investors.
He said the listed companies themselves also had a responsibility to keep track of their shareholders.
